limitations: BNCI and Shin have different identities, training/preprocessing, enrollment sizes, stream budgets and session roles; this is portability, not an exact replication or a controlled dataset effect.

Nine and 27 reused people are not untouched confirmation cohorts. Seeds reuse evaluation trials; rotations reuse people and exchange session roles. No independent-seed/cohort confidence interval or significance claim.

Fine symbols contain the hard decisions. Lower achieved confidence-symbol accuracy does not imply less available information or greater privacy; it can reflect limitations of the fixed attacker and transfer.

Hard-label streams still support identification in these descriptive means. One binary observation has a uniform-identity alphabet ceiling 2/N, but this one-symbol bound does not apply to a multi-output stream.
Confidence suppression preserves every task decision but removes confidence-dependent utility such as abstention. No general privacy, membership, bottleneck-mechanism or deployment-default claim.

The earlier Shin bottleneck noninferiority stop and BNCI nonlinear competence verdict remain unchanged; no stopped experiment was reopened. Both output-stream studies are closed without tuning or automatic extension.
method: Binary hard decisions versus sixteen symbols containing the decision and eight fixed equally spaced winning-confidence bands on [0.5,1]. Per-identity fine-symbol counts use pseudocount one. Hard-label counts and pseudocount eight are exact marginals of the fine table. Uniform identity prior; fixed conditional-independent product likelihood ignoring order; exact integer-product comparison, ties to lowest enrolled numeric identity. All enrollment tables were committed before evaluation identity scoring. No parameter, seed or budget search. Balanced per-identity evaluation counts make BA equal correct/number-of-bags; classes are also balanced for the task BA. These attack evaluations required zero new EEG fits, zero EEG inference and zero data downloads.
scope: Curated aggregate arithmetic for two completed output-stream studies, not a complete attack/data reproduction bundle or a new frozen release. Public verification recounts means, denominators and paired differences from model-level integer successes; it cannot independently regenerate enrollment tables, symbols or individual predictions. Source-summary hashes identify the audited originals; the originals contain additional nonpublic provenance. No raw EEG, per-person outputs, weights, posterior streams or identity tables are redistributed.

studies.protocol: Four retained current-runtime plain EEGNet models; native 0train enrollment to 1test evaluation. Enrollment uses all 144 source-session outputs per identity. K12 splits each native 24-trial run into two nonoverlapping halves without crossing a run or identity. From cached binary logits, band=min(7,floor(8*tanh(abs(logit1-logit0)/2))); symbol=8*argmax+band. Exact argmax ties select class zero.

Twelve original plain compact-EEGNet models; three native session rotations (enrollment/unused validation/evaluation): 0imagery/2imagery/4imagery, 2imagery/4imagery/0imagery, 4imagery/0imagery/2imagery. Enrollment uses all twenty task-training-session outputs per identity, including sixteen gradient-training and four reserved rows. K10 uses two nonoverlapping halves per identity in original cache order, not verified chronological adjacency. Normalize cached float32 binary probabilities in float64, then band=min(7,floor(16*(winning confidence-0.5))); symbol=8*argmax+band. Row sums must be within 1e-5 of one. Exact argmax ties select class zero.

threat_model: Passive observer sees only emitted task symbols from one plain model, has identity-labeled enrollment outputs and knows every target bag belongs to one of the enrolled people. Known same-person grouping is auxiliary information. No EEG/query inputs, true task labels, timestamps, routing/device/run identifiers, embeddings, weights, adaptive queries or combined outputs from multiple models. Protected object is identity, not membership.
